title: TE-2 — Table Detail Eligibility Directive Delivery
summary: recognise the exact table-detail comment next to one Markdown table and project the marker consumed by Content Detail View while every other comment harmlessly no-ops
content_html:
TE-2 — Table Detail Eligibility Directive Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as TE-2, after TE-1 provides convenient comment insertion, and required before TE-3 table integration. Authoring Directives Concept And Examples owns the exact-comment, next-table, working-source, projection, and harmless no-op boundaries implemented by this delivery.

TE-2 adds one deliberately small consumer: an author marks an exact Markdown table as eligible for Content Detail View. The build recognises that exact comment immediately before a table and annotates the rendered semantic table. Every other comment is ignored, and the browser never parses comments or decides whether a table is large enough.

Complete Outcome

The initial source form is:

<!-- dotlineform:table-detail -->

| Project | Folder | Series |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nerve | projects/nerve | Series 105 |

Canonical Markdown and Markdown export retain the comment. Supported rendered payloads contain the same semantic table with data-docs-content-detail="table"; retaining the ordinary invisible HTML comment is acceptable. Unmarked tables receive no marker and therefore no Open table control.

The document-level viewer_content_detail: table contract remains owned by TE-6. Its independent build behavior projects the same marker onto the sole eligible table without requiring a redundant comment. If another comment intervenes between table-detail and the table, table-detail simply does not associate and has no effect.

Current Seams And Expected Size

The likely owners are narrow Markdown source recognition, existing Markdown rendering, item-payload construction, full and targeted Docs builds, public/local payload parity, export behavior, and focused builder tests. TE-3 separately owns the runtime adapter that consumes the projected marker.

The current indicative shape is 3–6 touched production files, approximately 140–280 production Python lines and 180–320 focused test lines. TE-2.0 must replace this estimate with exact recognition, association, payload, export, and test files. If the work requires a central directive parser, diagnostics framework, browser parser, Markdown AST replacement, source mutation, or materially exceeds the estimate, stop for review.

Rough Delivery Steps

TE-2.0 — Trace And Freeze Exact Recognition

  • [ ] Trace HTML-comment preservation, Markdown table recognition, renderer tokens or source positions, item-payload construction, full/targeted builds, Markdown/static export, source copying, and current public/local content parity.
  • [ ] Freeze the one accepted <!-- dotlineform:table-detail --> shape, allowed blank lines, next-table association, and the rule that any intervening non-blank block leaves the comment inert.
  • [ ] Freeze the exact projected marker, implicit marker from viewer_content_detail: table, authored-attribute collision behavior, and ordinary-table fallback for every unrecognised or unassociated comment.
  • [ ] Record exact production/test files, reused Markdown-rendering seams, and rough diffs for TE-2.1 and TE-2.2 before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: one fixture contains ordinary HTML comments, an unmarked table, two independently detail-marked tables, a document-default single table, malformed lookalikes, an intervening block, a missing table, and stacked comments. Dry-run output demonstrates exact source association, marker projection, and ordinary semantic fallback without build errors or changed cell HTML. Stop before implementation.

TE-2.1 — Recognise, Associate, And Project

  • [ ] Recognise only the exact maintained comment without interpreting ordinary HTML comments or attempting to classify malformed lookalikes.
  • [ ] Associate it with one immediately following source Markdown table through maintained renderer/source-position seams rather than matching rendered HTML.
  • [ ] Project only data-docs-content-detail="table" onto the associated semantic table without requiring comment removal.
  • [ ] Preserve canonical Markdown, Markdown export, table cell HTML, links, alignment, headings, captions, unrelated authored attributes, and ordinary rendering for every no-op case.
  • [ ] Apply the same marker independently for the TE-6 document-default case; if its own validation does not apply, leave the ordinary document unchanged through that feature’s fallback.

TE-2.2 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused exact-match, association, ordinary-comment, malformed-lookalike, unmarked/marked table, implicit document-default, stacked-comment, full/targeted build, local/public payload, export, lint, generated Docs/search, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Prove only intended semantic tables receive the exact marker and every other comment/table combination builds normally.
  • [ ] Prove documents without directives remain byte-equivalent apart from any unavoidable maintained renderer normalization.
  • [ ] Update the concise Markdown authoring and payload contracts, then hand the projected marker to TE-3 without implementing Content Detail runtime behavior or a directive diagnostics system here.

Not In Scope

  • scanning table size, overflow, row count, headings, or viewport state;
  • adding Open table, Content Detail lifecycle, cloning, layout, toolbar, or Back behavior owned by TE-3;
  • table-to-SVG comment recognition, rendering, manifests, media, or public replacement owned by TE-7;
  • the Source toolbar action for inserting comments, already owned by TE-1;
  • validation or reporting for unknown, malformed, misplaced, duplicate, contradictory, or unsupported comments;
  • a general directive registry, reserved-name catalogue, runtime comment metadata, or browser comment parser;
  • applying directives to dynamic report/component tables or arbitrary HTML; or
  • stable table URLs, IDs, occurrence numbers, or persistent runtime identity.

The Table Enhancements feature owns the sequence. TE-3 begins its table integration only after TE-2 supplies exact marker projection and focused evidence.
